# Latex Fit Lab — latex clothing size, fit and thickness

> Free tools for latex clothing: a size calculator that turns body measurements into the finished
> measurements a maker should cut, a measuring guide and a thickness guide.

Latex has no sizing standard, so makers work from finished measurements rather than size letters.
Latex Fit Lab publishes the reduction values as numbers, so a customer and a maker can agree on the
same sheet.

## Key pages
- [Latex size calculator](https://latex-tools.pages.dev/size-calculator/): nine body measurements in, finished garment measurements out, with a copy-ready sheet to send to a maker.
- [How to measure for latex clothing](https://latex-tools.pages.dev/measure-guide/): the nine measurements a maker needs and the three that go wrong most often.
- [Latex thickness guide](https://latex-tools.pages.dev/thickness-guide/): 0.25 mm to 1.00 mm sheeting, what each thickness is for and how much smaller it is cut.
- [Home](https://latex-tools.pages.dev/): overview of the three tools.

## Facts
- Latex clothing has no sizing standard and no universal size chart; the working numbers are finished garment measurements.
- Latex is cut smaller than the body ("negative ease"). Base reduction by sheeting thickness: 0.25 mm 14-17%, 0.40 mm 12-15%, 0.60 mm 10-13%, 0.80 mm 8-11%, 1.00 mm 6-9%.
- Thicker sheeting stretches less, so it is cut with less reduction, not more.
- Per-part adjustment on top of the base reduction, in percentage points: thigh +2, upper arm +2, waist +1, chest 0, hip 0, underbust −1, neck −5.
- Torso length is cut 2-4% shorter than the body measurement.
- Fit preference shifts every value by 2 points: relaxed −2, snug +2.
- A latex garment is measured with a soft tailor's tape, over the body, in the order given in the measuring guide.
